title: Visualization Design MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Design your own chart of a restaurant tips dataset by choosing the chart type, the columns, a color grouping, and a title, and watch the preview, the Plotly Express code, and a design check update together.

educational.topic: Designing a chart with Plotly Express
learningObjectives: Students will be able to design a chart for a question about a dataset by selecting a chart type, columns, color grouping, and title, and justify the design.
prerequisites: Scatter, line, bar, histogram, and box plots
Calling px functions with x, y, and color

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Open-ended design with a live preview, generated code, and rule-based feedback
keyQuestions: Why does the line chart of tip against total_bill look like a scribble?
What does the height of a bar mean when x is day and y is tip?
How does adding a color column change both the chart and the code?
What makes a title useful to someone seeing the chart for the first time?
commonMisconceptions: Any chart type works for any pair of columns (the type has to match whether the columns are numeric or categorical).
A bar chart of tip by day shows the average tip (px.bar adds up the rows, so it shows the total).
A histogram needs a y column (it counts rows in bins of x).
A line chart is just a scatter plot with the dots connected (the connections claim an order that this data does not have).
assessmentOpportunities: Students write their own question about the tips data, build a chart that answers it with no warnings in the design check, and hand in the generated code with two sentences that justify the chart type and the title.
